haem.m: A complex red organic pigment containing iron and other atoms to which oxygen binds.

haemagglutinate.m: Cause the clumping together (of red blood cells).

haemal.m: Relating to the blood vessels or blood.

haemangioma.m: Benign angioma consisting of a mass of blood vessels; some appear as birthmarks.

haemangiomas.m: Benign angioma consisting of a mass of blood vessels; some appear as birthmarks.

haematic.m: Relating to or containing or affecting blood.

haematinics.m: A medicine that increases the hemoglobin content of the blood; used to treat iron-deficiency anemia.

haematite.m: The principal form of iron ore; consists of ferric oxide in crystalline form; occurs in a red earthy form.

haematocele.m: Swelling caused by blood collecting in a body cavity (especially a swelling of the membrane covering the testis).

haematoceles.m: Swelling caused by blood collecting in a body cavity (especially a swelling of the membrane covering the testis).

haematocrit.m: The ratio of the volume occupied by packed red blood cells to the volume of the whole blood as measured by a hematocrit.

haematocrits.m: The ratio of the volume occupied by packed red blood cells to the volume of the whole blood as measured by a hematocrit.

haematogenesis.m: The formation of blood cells in the living body (especially in the bone marrow).

haematological.m: Of or relating to or involved in hematology.

haematologist.m: A doctor who specialises in diseases of the blood and blood-forming organs.

haematologists.m: A doctor who specialises in diseases of the blood and blood-forming organs.

haematology.m: The branch of medicine that deals with diseases of the blood and blood-forming organs.

haematoma.m: A localised swelling filled with blood.

haematomas.m: A localised swelling filled with blood.

haematomata.m: A localised swelling filled with blood.

haematopoiesis.m: The formation of blood cells in the living body (especially in the bone marrow).

haematopoietic.m: Pertaining to the formation of blood or blood cells.

haematuria.m: The presence of blood in the urine; often a symptom of urinary tract disease.

haemic.m: Relating to or containing or affecting blood.

haemodialyses.m: Dialysis of the blood to remove toxic substances or metabolic wastes from the bloodstream; used in the case of kidney failure.

haemodialysis.m: Dialysis of the blood to remove toxic substances or metabolic wastes from the bloodstream; used in the case of kidney failure.

haemoglobin.m: A hemoprotein composed of globin and heme that gives red blood cells their characteristic colour; function primarily to transport oxygen from the lungs to the body tissues.

haemoglobinopathies.m: A blood disease characterised by the presence of abnormal hemoglobins in the blood.

haemoglobinopathy.m: A blood disease characterised by the presence of abnormal hemoglobins in the blood.

haemoglobinuria.m: Presence of hemoglobin in the urine.

haemolysin.m: Any substance that can cause lysis (destruction) of erythrocytes (red blood cells) and the release of their hemoglobin.

haemolysis.m: Lysis of erythrocytes with the release of hemoglobin.

haemolytic.m: Relating to or involving or causing hemolysis.

haemophilia.m: Congenital tendency to uncontrolled bleeding; usually affects males and is transmitted from mother to son.

haemophiliac.m: Someone who has hemophilia and is subject to uncontrollable bleeding.

haemophiliacs.m: Someone who has hemophilia and is subject to uncontrollable bleeding.

haemoptyses.m: Coughing up blood from the respiratory tract; usually indicates a severe infection of the bronchi or lungs.

haemoptysis.m: Coughing up blood from the respiratory tract; usually indicates a severe infection of the bronchi or lungs.

haemorrhage.m: The flow of blood from a ruptured blood vessel.

haemorrhages.m: The flow of blood from a ruptured blood vessel.

haemorrhoidectomy.m: Surgical procedure for tying hemorrhoids and excising them.

haemostasia.m: Surgical procedure of stopping the flow of blood (as with a hemostat).

haemostasis.m: Surgical procedure of stopping the flow of blood (as with a hemostat).

haemostat.m: A surgical instrument that stops bleeding by clamping the blood vessel.
